name: Non-zero Segments
description: Kolya got an integer array $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$. The array can contain both positive and negative integers, but Kolya doesn't like $$$0$$$, so the array doesn't contain any zeros. Kolya doesn't like that the sum of some subsegments of his array can be $$$0$$$. The subsegment is some consecutive segment of elements of the array. You have to help Kolya and change his array in such a way that it doesn't contain any subsegments with the sum $$$0$$$. To reach this goal, you can insert any integers between any pair of adjacent elements of the array (integers can be really any: positive, negative, $$$0$$$, any by absolute value, even such a huge that they can't be represented in most standard programming languages). Your task is to find the minimum number of integers you have to insert into Kolya's array in such a way that the resulting array doesn't contain any subsegments with the sum $$$0$$$.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 200\,000$$$) — the number of elements in Kolya's array. The second line of the input contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$-10^{9} \le a_i \le 10^{9}, a_i \neq 0$$$) — the description of Kolya's array.
output_specification: Print the minimum number of integers you have to insert into Kolya's array in such a way that the resulting array doesn't contain any subsegments with the sum $$$0$$$.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1426D — Non-zero Segments [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
